=== README ===
# neuvector-mcp
[![FOSSA Status](https://app.fossa.com/api/projects/git%2Bgithub.com%2Fdarthzen%2Fneuvector-mcp.svg?type=shield)](https://app.fossa.com/projects/git%2Bgithub.com%2Fdarthzen%2Fneuvector-mcp?ref=badge_shield)


A Model Context Protocol server over the SUSE NeuVector container security
control plane. It exposes NeuVector's inventory, vulnerability, compliance,
event and policy surface as 119 typed MCP tools, so an operator or an agent can
ask questions like *"which prod workloads run images with critical CVEs and are
still in Discover mode"* and, behind an explicit two-step confirmation, act on
the answer. It ships as one SUSE BCI image that runs either over `stdio` for
a desktop MCP client or over authenticated HTTP in-cluster.

**Read-only by default.** Of the 119 tools, only the 52 read tools are registered
unless you deliberately turn a mutating toolset on.

---

## Contents

- [Quick start — stdio](#quick-start--stdio)
- [Quick start — in-cluster HTTP](#quick-start--in-cluster-http)
- [Configuration](#configuration)
- [Toolsets](#toolsets)
- [The confirmation handshake](#the-confirmation-handshake)
- [NeuVector API key provisioning](#neuvector-api-key-provisioning)
- [Verified vs unverified](#verified-vs-unverified)
- [Known issues](#known-issues)
- [Running the gate](#running-the-gate)

---

## Quick start — stdio

`stdio` inherits the trust boundary of the parent process, so it carries no
transport auth. Use it only for a local desktop client.

Four environment variables and one command:

```bash
export NV_CONTROLLER_URL=https://<controller-host>:10443
export NV_API_ACCESS_KEY=<apikey_name>
export NV_API_SECRET_KEY=<apikey_secret>
export NV_VERIFY_TLS=false      # the controller serves a self-signed cert by default

neuvector-mcp
```

`NV_TRANSPORT` defaults to `stdio` and `NV_READ_ONLY` defaults to `true`, so the
above gives you the 52 read tools and nothing else.

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling>=1.27"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[project]
name = "neuvector-mcp"
version = "1.1.2"
description = "Model Context Protocol server for the SUSE NeuVector container security platform"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
license = { text = "Apache-2.0" }
dependencies = [
  "fastmcp==3.4.5",
  "httpx==0.28.1",
  "pydantic==2.13.4",
  "structlog==26.1.0",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = [
  "pytest==8.4.2",
  "pytest-asyncio==1.4.0",
  "pytest-cov==7.0.0",
  "respx==0.23.1",
  "mypy==1.18.2",
  "ruff==0.14.4",
]

[project.scripts]
neuvector-mcp = "neuvector_mcp.server:main"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/neuvector_mcp"]

# --- test ---------------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
testpaths = ["tests"]
pythonpath = ["src", "tests"]
addopts = "-q --strict-markers --strict-config"
filterwarnings = ["error::DeprecationWarning:neuvector_mcp.*"]

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["neuvector_mcp"]
branch = true

[tool.coverage.report]
fail_under = 85
show_missing = true
exclude_lines = ["pragma: no cover", "if TYPE_CHECKING:", "raise NotImplementedError"]

# --- lint ---------------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py312"
src = ["src", "tests"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "I", "N", "UP", "B", "A", "C4", "T20", "SIM", "RUF", "ASYNC", "S"]
ignore = [
  "S101",   # assert is how tests assert
  "N818",   # trailing-underscore error names are deliberate (PermissionError_)
  "B008",   # Field() in Annotated defaults is the FastMCP idiom
  # E501 cannot be enforced against this spec, for three independent reasons:
  #   1. Gate rule R6 parses `Calls <METHOD> <path>` out of every tool docstring
  #      with a regex that requires method+path on ONE physical line. Several
  #      exceed 100 columns and cannot be wrapped without failing the gate.
  #   2. `Field(description=...)` text is the tool contract a client model reads
  #      (SPEC 7.5/7.6). Reflowing it to fit a column limit is a real cost for a
  #      cosmetic gain.
  #   3. The worst offenders are in scripts/verify_spec.py and client.py, which
  #      SPEC N3 requires be kept verbatim -- so zero E501 is unreachable anyway.
  # `ruff format` still wraps everything it safely can; this only silences the
  # residue it cannot split (strings and comments).
  "E501",   # see above -- spec-verbatim docstrings + R6's single-line requirement
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/**" = ["S105", "S106", "T201"]
"scripts/**" = ["T201"]
# The entries below are all files SPEC rule N3 requires be kept VERBATIM from
# reference/. They are copied, not authored here, so a lint finding in one of
# them cannot be fixed without violating N3. Scoped per-file (and per-rule) so
# these exemptions never mask the same finding in code we do own.
"scripts/verify_spec.py" = ["T201", "B905"]
"src/neuvector_mcp/client.py" = [
  "S105",    # "_TOKEN_HEADER" is a header NAME, not a credential
  "SIM105",  # try/except/pass on best-effort logout is deliberate
  "SIM108",  # explicit if/else for the ca_bundle/verify_tls precedence reads clearer
]
"src/neuvector_mcp/config.py" = ["S104"]  # 0.0.0.0 is the documented NV_HTTP_HOST default
"src/neuvector_mcp/errors.py" = ["N801"]  # PermissionError_/ValidationError_ avoid shadowing builtins
"tests/conftest.py" = ["C408"]

# --- types --------------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.12"
files = ["src", "scripts"]
strict = true
warn_unreachable = true
disallow_untyped_decorators = false   # FastMCP decorators are untyped upstream

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["respx.*", "structlog.*"]
ignore_missing_imports = true

# Same rationale as the ruff per-file-ignores above: these are verbatim copies
# from reference/ under SPEC N3, so their strict-mode findings cannot be fixed
# here. Narrowed to the specific error codes each file actually trips, so a NEW
# class of type error in these modules still fails the build.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["neuvector_mcp.client"]
disable_error_code = ["assignment", "unreachable"]

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["neuvector_mcp.context"]
disable_error_code = ["union-attr"]

# verify_spec.py introspects FastMCP's tool objects, which are typed `object`
# upstream; every access is guarded at runtime by the gate's own checks.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["verify_spec"]
disable_error_code = ["attr-defined"]

.DEFAULT_GOAL := help
PY      ?= python3
IMAGE   ?= neuvector-mcp
TAG     ?= 1.1.2
REGISTRY?= localhost:5000

.PHONY: help
help: ## show targets
	@grep -hE '^[a-zA-Z_-]+:.*?## ' $(MAKEFILE_LIST) | awk 'BEGIN{FS=":.*?## "}{printf "  \033[36m%-16s\033[0m %s\n",$$1,$$2}'

.PHONY: install
install: ## install the package plus dev extras into the active environment
	$(PY) -m pip install -e '.[dev]'

.PHONY: lint
lint: ## ruff check + format check
	$(PY) -m ruff check src tests scripts
	$(PY) -m ruff format --check src tests scripts

.PHONY: fmt
fmt: ## apply ruff formatting
	$(PY) -m ruff check --fix src tests scripts
	$(PY) -m ruff format src tests scripts

.PHONY: types
types: ## strict mypy
	$(PY) -m mypy

.PHONY: test
test: ## unit + contract tests with coverage gate
	$(PY) -m pytest --cov --cov-report=term-missing

.PHONY: spec
spec: ## machine-checkable spec compliance gate
	$(PY) scripts/verify_spec.py

.PHONY: smoke
smoke: ## start over stdio against a live controller and list tools
	$(PY) scripts/smoke_stdio.py

.PHONY: verify
verify: lint types test spec ## the full gate; CI runs exactly this
	@echo "VERIFY OK"

.PHONY: image
image: ## build the container image on SUSE BCI
	podman build -t $(REGISTRY)/$(IMAGE):$(TAG) -f deploy/Dockerfile .

.PHONY: clean
clean:
	rm -rf .pytest_cache .mypy_cache .ruff_cache .coverage htmlcov dist build
	find . -name __pycache__ -type d -prune -exec rm -rf {} +

1	"""Async HTTP client for the NeuVector controller REST API.
2	
3	Responsibilities, and nothing else:
4	
5	* hold one :class:`httpx.AsyncClient` for the process lifetime
6	* attach the correct auth header on every request
7	* re-login exactly once when the controller rejects a session token
8	* apply the NeuVector query conventions (``start``/``limit``/``f_*``/``s_*``)
9	* convert non-2xx responses into typed exceptions from :mod:`.errors`
10	* never log a secret
11	
12	Auth header rules (source: controller/rest/auth.go ``restReq2User``):
13	
14	* API key:  ``X-Auth-Apikey: <access_key>:<secret_key>``  (stateless, no login)
15	* Password: ``POST /v1/auth`` then ``X-Auth-Token: <token>`` on later calls
16	
17	The controller checks ``X-Auth-Token`` first and only falls back to
18	``X-Auth-Apikey``. Never send both.
19	"""
20	
21	from __future__ import annotations
22	
23	import asyncio
24	import ssl
25	from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
26	from typing import Any, Literal
27	
28	import httpx
29	import structlog
30

32	from .errors import AuthError, NeuVectorMCPError, UpstreamError, classify, is_retryable
33	
34	log = structlog.get_logger(__name__)
35	
36	Method = Literal["GET", "POST", "PATCH", "DELETE"]
37	
38	#: NeuVector filter comparison operators (controller/api/apis.go).
39	FILTER_OPS: frozenset[str] = frozenset(
40	    {"eq", "neq", "in", "notin", "gt", "gte", "lt", "lte", "prefix"}
41	)
42	
43	_TOKEN_HEADER = "X-Auth-Token"
44	_APIKEY_HEADER = "X-Auth-Apikey"
45	_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3
46	_BACKOFF_BASE_S = 0.5

48	
49	def build_query(
50	    *,
51	    start: int | None = None,
52	    limit: int | None = None,
53	    filters: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
54	    sort: Mapping[str, Literal["asc", "desc"]] | None = None,
55	    extra: Mapping[str, str | int | bool] | None = None,
56	) -> dict[str, str]:
57	    """Render NeuVector query parameters.
58	
59	    Filters use the ``f_<field>`` convention. A value may be a bare literal
60	    (implicit ``eq``) or ``"<op>,<value>"`` where ``<op>`` is one of
61	    :data:`FILTER_OPS`. Sorts use ``s_<field>=asc|desc``.
62	
63	    Args:
64	        start: Zero-based offset. Negative values page backwards (controller
65	            behaviour), so callers that only want forward paging pass >= 0.
66	        limit: Maximum items to return. ``0`` means "controller default".
67	        filters: ``{"domain": "prod"}`` or ``{"cvedb_version": "gte,2024.1"}``.
68	        sort: ``{"reported_at": "desc"}``.
69	        extra: Endpoint-specific pairs such as ``{"scope": "local"}`` or
70	            ``{"view": "pod"}``.
71	
72	    Returns:
73	        A flat ``dict[str, str]`` suitable for ``httpx``' ``params=``.
74	
75	    Raises:
76	        ValueError: if a filter names an unknown comparison operator.
77	    """
78	    params: dict[str, str] = {}
79	    if start is not None:
80	        params["start"] = str(start)
81	    if limit is not None:
82	        params["limit"] = str(limit)
83	    for field, value in (filters or {}).items():
84	        text = str(value)
85	        if "," in text:
86	            op, _, rest = text.partition(",")
87	            if op not in FILTER_OPS:
88	                raise ValueError(
89	                    f"filter {field!r} uses unknown operator {op!r}; "
90	                    f"valid operators: {sorted(FILTER_OPS)}"
91	                )
92	            text = f"{op},{rest}"
93	        params[f"f_{field}"] = text
94	    for field, direction in (sort or {}).items():
95	        if direction not in ("asc", "desc"):
96	            raise ValueError(f"sort {field!r} must be 'asc' or 'desc', got {direction!r}")
97	        params[f"s_{field}"] = direction
98	    for key, value in (extra or {}).items():
99	        params[key] = str(value).lower() if isinstance(value, bool) else str(value)
100	    return params

105	
106	    def __init__(self, settings: Settings, http: httpx.AsyncClient) -> None:
107	        self._s = settings
108	        self._http = http
109	        self._token: str | None = None
110	        self._login_lock = asyncio.Lock()
111	        #: Global permissions of the current identity, filled in by :meth:`login`.
112	        self.identity: dict[str, Any] = {}
113	
114	    # -- construction -----------------------------------------------------------
115	    @classmethod
116	    def build_http_client(cls, settings: Settings) -> httpx.AsyncClient:
117	        """Create the underlying ``httpx.AsyncClient`` for these settings."""
118	        verify: bool | ssl.SSLContext | str
119	        if settings.ca_bundle:
120	            verify = settings.ca_bundle
121	        else:
122	            verify = settings.verify_tls
123	        return httpx.AsyncClient(
124	            base_url=settings.controller_url,
125	            verify=verify,
126	            timeout=httpx.Timeout(settings.request_timeout_s),
127	            headers={"Content-Type": "application/json", "Accept": "application/json"},
128	            follow_redirects=False,
129	        )
130	
131	    # -- authentication ---------------------------------------------------------
132	    async def login(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
133	        """Establish an identity against the controller.
134	
135	        In ``apikey`` mode no login request is made; the API key is stateless, so
136	        this method probes ``GET /v1/system/summary`` to fail fast on bad keys.
137	
138	        In ``password`` mode this posts ``RESTAuthData`` to ``POST /v1/auth`` and
139	        caches the returned token.
140	
141	        Returns:
142	            A dict with ``mode``, ``username`` and ``global_permissions``.
143	
144	        Raises:
145	            AuthError: on rejected credentials.
146	        """
147	        if self._s.auth_mode == "apikey":
148	            await self.request("GET", "/v1/system/summary", authenticated=True)
149	            self.identity = {
150	                "mode": "apikey",
151	                "username": self._s.api_access_key,
152	                "global_permissions": ["unknown (api key)"],
153	            }
154	            return self.identity
155	
156	        payload = {
157	            "password": {
158	                "username": self._s.username,
159	                "password": self._s.password,
160	            }
161	        }
162	        response = await self._http.post("/v1/auth", json=payload)
163	        if response.status_code != 200:
164	            raise classify(response.status_code, _safe_json(response))
165	        token_data = response.json().get("token") or {}
166	        token = token_data.get("token")
167	        if not token:
168	            raise AuthError("POST /v1/auth succeeded but returned no token")
169	        self._token = token
170	        self.identity = {
171	            "mode": "password",
172	            "username": token_data.get("fullname") or self._s.username,
173	            "global_permissions": [
174	                p.get("id") for p in (token_data.get("global_permissions") or [])
175	            ],
176	        }
177	        log.info("nv.login", mode="password", username=self.identity["username"])
178	        return self.identity
179	
180	    async def logout(self) -> None:
181	        """Invalidate a password-mode session token. No-op for API keys."""
182	        if self._s.auth_mode == "password" and self._token:
183	            try:
184	                await self._http.delete("/v1/auth", headers=self._auth_headers())
185	            except httpx.HTTPError:  # pragma: no cover - best effort
186	                pass
187	            self._token = None
188	
189	    def _auth_headers(self) -> dict[str, str]:
190	        if self._s.auth_mode == "apikey":
191	            return {_APIKEY_HEADER: f"{self._s.api_access_key}:{self._s.api_secret_key}"}
192	        if self._token:
193	            return {_TOKEN_HEADER: self._token}
194	        return {}
195	
196	    # -- request path -----------------------------------------------------------
197	    async def request(
198	        self,
199	        method: Method,
200	        path: str,
201	        *,
202	        params: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
203	        json: Any | None = None,
204	        timeout_s: float | None = None,
205	        authenticated: bool = True,
206	        _relogin_done: bool = False,
207	    ) -> Any:
208	        """Perform one controller call and return the parsed JSON body.
209	
210	        Args:
211	            method: HTTP verb.
212	            path: Absolute controller path beginning with ``/v1/`` or ``/v2/``.
213	            params: Query parameters, normally produced by :func:`build_query`.
214	            json: Request body, already shaped as the controller's ``REST*Data``.
215	            timeout_s: Per-call override; use
216	                ``settings.long_request_timeout_s`` for scan and bench calls.
217	            authenticated: Set ``False`` only for ``POST /v1/auth``.
218	            _relogin_done: Internal recursion guard.
219	
220	        Returns:
221	            Parsed JSON, or ``{}`` when the controller returns an empty body
222	            (common for ``PATCH``/``DELETE``).
223	
224	        Raises:
225	            NeuVectorMCPError: for every non-2xx response, already classified.
226	        """
227	        headers = self._auth_headers() if authenticated else {}
228	        attempt = 0
229	        last_exc: NeuVectorMCPError | None = None
230	
231	        while attempt < _MAX_ATTEMPTS:
232	            attempt += 1
233	            try:
234	                response = await self._http.request(
235	                    method,
236	                    path,
237	                    params=dict(params or {}),
238	                    json=json,
239	                    headers=headers,
240	                    timeout=timeout_s or self._s.request_timeout_s,
241	                )
242	            except httpx.TimeoutException as exc:
243	                last_exc = UpstreamError(f"controller timeout on {method} {path}: {exc}")
244	            except httpx.HTTPError as exc:
245	                last_exc = UpstreamError(f"controller unreachable on {method} {path}: {exc}")
246	            else:
247	                if 200 <= response.status_code < 300:
248	                    return _safe_json(response) or {}
249	                body = _safe_json(response)
250	                if (
251	                    response.status_code == 401
252	                    and self._s.auth_mode == "password"
253	                    and not _relogin_done
254	                ):
255	                    async with self._login_lock:
256	                        await self.login()
257	                    return await self.request(
258	                        method,
259	                        path,
260	                        params=params,
261	                        json=json,
262	                        timeout_s=timeout_s,
263	                        authenticated=authenticated,
264	                        _relogin_done=True,
265	                    )
266	                if not is_retryable(response.status_code, body):
267	                    raise classify(response.status_code, body)
268	                last_exc = classify(response.status_code, body)
269	
270	            if attempt < _MAX_ATTEMPTS:
271	                await asyncio.sleep(_BACKOFF_BASE_S * (2 ** (attempt - 1)))
272	
273	        raise last_exc or UpstreamError(f"{method} {path} failed after {_MAX_ATTEMPTS} attempts")
274	
275	    # -- convenience ------------------------------------------------------------
276	    async def get_list(
277	        self,
278	        path: str,
279	        envelope_key: str,
280	        *,
281	        params: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
282	    ) -> list[Any]:
283	        """GET a list endpoint and unwrap its envelope key.
284	
285	        NeuVector wraps collections, e.g. ``GET /v1/group`` returns
286	        ``{"groups": [...]}``. Returns ``[]`` when the key is absent or null.
287	        """
288	        body = await self.request("GET", path, params=params)
289	        value = body.get(envelope_key) if isinstance(body, dict) else None
290	        return list(value) if isinstance(value, Sequence) and not isinstance(value, str) else []
291	
292	    async def get_object(
293	        self, path: str, envelope_key: str, *, params: Mapping[str, str] | None = None
294	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
295	        """GET a single-object endpoint and unwrap its envelope key."""
296	        body = await self.request("GET", path, params=params)
297	        value = body.get(envelope_key) if isinstance(body, dict) else None
298	        return dict(value) if isinstance(value, Mapping) else {}
299	
300	
301	def _safe_json(response: httpx.Response) -> Any:
302	    """Parse a response body as JSON, returning ``None`` when it is not JSON."""
303	    if not response.content:
304	        return None
305	    try:
306	        return response.json()
307	    except ValueError:
308	        return response.text[:500]

192	def load_settings() -> Settings:
193	    """Build :class:`Settings` from the process environment.
194	
195	    Raises:
196	        pydantic.ValidationError: if the environment is incomplete or contradictory.
197	    """
198	    toolsets_raw = _env("TOOLSETS")
199	    toolsets = (
200	        tuple(t.strip() for t in toolsets_raw.split(",") if t.strip())
201	        if toolsets_raw
202	        else DEFAULT_TOOLSETS
203	    )
204	
205	    tokens_raw = _env("HTTP_BEARER_TOKENS", "")
206	    bearer: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
207	    for entry in (tokens_raw or "").split(","):
208	        entry = entry.strip()
209	        if not entry:
210	            continue
211	        token, _, scopes = entry.partition(":")
212	        bearer[token] = [s for s in scopes.split("|") if s] or ["nv:read"]
213	
214	    return Settings(
215	        controller_url=_env("CONTROLLER_URL", "https://127.0.0.1:10443") or "",
216	        verify_tls=_env_bool("VERIFY_TLS", True),
217	        ca_bundle=_env("CA_BUNDLE"),
218	        request_timeout_s=float(_env("REQUEST_TIMEOUT_S", "30") or 30),
219	        long_request_timeout_s=float(_env("LONG_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_S", "300") or 300),
220	        auth_mode=_env("AUTH_MODE", "apikey"),  # type: ignore[arg-type]
221	        api_access_key=_env("API_ACCESS_KEY"),
222	        api_secret_key=_env("API_SECRET_KEY"),
223	        username=_env("USERNAME"),
224	        password=_env("PASSWORD"),
225	        transport=_env("TRANSPORT", "stdio"),  # type: ignore[arg-type]
226	        http_host=_env("HTTP_HOST", "0.0.0.0") or "0.0.0.0",
227	        http_port=_env_int("HTTP_PORT", 8080),
228	        http_path=_env("HTTP_PATH", "/mcp") or "/mcp",
229	        http_bearer_tokens=bearer,
230	        read_only=_env_bool("READ_ONLY", True),
231	        toolsets=toolsets,
232	        require_confirm_token=_env_bool("REQUIRE_CONFIRM_TOKEN", True),
233	        allow_undocumented=_env_bool("ALLOW_UNDOCUMENTED", False),
234	        allowed_namespaces=tuple(

1	"""Write guard: the only place a mutating call may be authorised.
2	
3	Every mutating tool calls :func:`authorise_write` before it touches the client.
4	The guard enforces four independent conditions, in this order:
5	
6	1. ``NV_READ_ONLY`` must be false.
7	2. The tool's toolset must be enabled in ``NV_TOOLSETS``.
8	3. When ``NV_ALLOWED_NAMESPACES`` is non-empty, the target namespace must be in it.
9	4. When ``NV_REQUIRE_CONFIRM_TOKEN`` is true, the caller must echo back a
10	   deterministic confirmation token derived from the exact operation.
11	
12	Condition 4 makes accidental writes structurally impossible: the model cannot
13	guess the token, so it must first call the tool without one, read the returned
14	plan, and call again with the token. That two-step handshake is the audit trail.
15	"""
16	
17	from __future__ import annotations
18	
19	import hashlib
20	import json
21	from collections.abc import Mapping
22	from typing import Any
23	
24	from .config import Settings
25	from .errors import GuardError
26	from .models import WriteOutcome
27	
28	
29	def confirm_token(operation: str, target: str, payload: Mapping[str, Any] | None) -> str:
30	    """Derive the confirmation token for one specific mutation.
31	
32	    The token is a function of the operation name, the target identifier and the
33	    canonical JSON form of the payload, so changing any field invalidates it.
34	
35	    Args:
36	        operation: Stable operation id, e.g. ``"nv_delete_group"``.
37	        target: The object this mutation acts on, e.g. ``"nv.prod.api"``.
38	        payload: Request body, or ``None`` for payload-free operations.
39	
40	    Returns:
41	        A 12-character lowercase hex token.
42	    """
43	    canonical = json.dumps(payload or {}, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))
44	    digest = hashlib.sha256(f"{operation}|{target}|{canonical}".encode()).hexdigest()
45	    return digest[:12]
46	
47	
48	def authorise_write(
49	    settings: Settings,
50	    *,
51	    operation: str,
52	    toolset: str,
53	    target: str,
54	    effect: str,
55	    payload: Mapping[str, Any] | None,
56	    confirm: str | None,
57	    namespace: str | None = None,
58	) -> WriteOutcome | None:
59	    """Decide whether one mutating call may proceed.
60	
61	    Args:
62	        settings: Active server settings.
63	        operation: Tool name, used in the token and the audit record.
64	        toolset: The tool's toolset tag, e.g. ``"policy_write"``.
65	        target: Human-readable identifier of the object being changed.
66	        effect: One-sentence description of what will change, for the plan.
67	        payload: The exact body that will be sent to the controller.
68	        confirm: Token supplied by the caller, or ``None`` on the first call.
69	        namespace: Namespace the change lands in, when the operation is scoped.
70	
71	    Returns:
72	        ``None`` when the caller may proceed, or a
73	        :class:`~neuvector_mcp.models.WriteOutcome` with
74	        ``status="confirmation_required"`` that the tool must return verbatim.
75	
76	    Raises:
77	        GuardError: when the operation is forbidden outright, or when the
78	            supplied token does not match.
79	    """
80	    if settings.read_only:
81	        raise GuardError(
82	            f"{operation} is a mutating operation and this server is running with "
83	            "NV_READ_ONLY=true. No request was sent to the controller."
84	        )
85	    if not settings.toolset_enabled(toolset):
86	        raise GuardError(
87	            f"{operation} belongs to toolset {toolset!r}, which is not enabled. "
88	            f"Enabled toolsets: {sorted(settings.toolsets)}."
89	        )
90	    if namespace and settings.allowed_namespaces and namespace not in settings.allowed_namespaces:
91	        raise GuardError(
92	            f"{operation} targets namespace {namespace!r}, which is outside "
93	            f"NV_ALLOWED_NAMESPACES ({sorted(settings.allowed_namespaces)})."
94	        )
95	
96	    expected = confirm_token(operation, target, payload)
97	    if not settings.require_confirm_token:
98	        return None
99	    if confirm is None:
100	        return WriteOutcome(
101	            status="confirmation_required",
102	            operation=operation,
103	            target=target,
104	            effect=effect,
105	            payload=dict(payload or {}),
106	            confirm_token=expected,
107	            next_step=(
108	                f"Review 'effect' and 'payload'. To execute, call {operation} again "
109	                f"with identical arguments plus confirm={expected!r}."
110	            ),
111	        )
112	    if confirm != expected:
113	        raise GuardError(
114	            f"confirm token mismatch for {operation} on {target!r}. The arguments "
115	            "changed since the token was issued. Call again without 'confirm' to "
116	            "get a fresh plan and token."
117	        )
118	    return None
119

74	INSTRUCTIONS = """\
75	NeuVector container security control plane.
76	
77	Read before acting:
78	- Resolve objects before operating on them. Workload ids come from
79	  nv_list_workloads; group names from nv_list_groups; registry names from
80	  nv_list_registries. Never guess an id.
81	- Every mutating tool is a two-step handshake. Call it once WITHOUT 'confirm' to
82	  get a plan describing the exact effect plus a confirm token, then call again
83	  with that token. A plan is not a change; nothing was sent to the controller.
84	- Policy mode meanings: Discover learns and allows, Monitor alerts only, Protect
85	  blocks. Moving a group to Protect can break a running application.
86	- Vulnerability and event queries can return very large result sets. Filter by
87	  namespace, severity or time window first, then page with 'start'.
88	- When a tool reports truncated=true, either narrow the filter or page; do not
89	  assume the returned set is complete.
90	"""

93	@contextlib.asynccontextmanager
94	async def lifespan(server: FastMCP) -> AsyncIterator[AppContext]:
95	    """Open the controller connection, verify credentials, hold it for the process."""
96	    settings: Settings = server._nv_settings  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
97	    http = NeuVectorClient.build_http_client(settings)
98	    client = NeuVectorClient(settings, http)
99	    try:
100	        identity = await client.login()
101	        log.info(
102	            "nv.connected",
103	            controller=settings.controller_url,
104	            auth_mode=settings.auth_mode,
105	            read_only=settings.read_only,
106	            toolsets=list(settings.toolsets),
107	        )
108	        yield AppContext(settings=settings, client=client, identity=identity)

110	        await client.logout()
111	        await http.aclose()

114	def _auth_provider(settings: Settings) -> AuthProvider | None:
115	    """Return the HTTP auth provider, or ``None`` for stdio.
116	
117	    stdio inherits the trust boundary of the parent process, so it carries no
118	    auth. HTTP is network-reachable and therefore MUST be authenticated: the
119	    server refuses to start on HTTP without at least one bearer token.
120	    """
121	    if settings.transport != "http":
122	        return None
123	    if not settings.http_bearer_tokens:
124	        from .errors import ConfigError
125	
126	        raise ConfigError(
127	            "NV_TRANSPORT=http requires NV_HTTP_BEARER_TOKENS "
128	            "(format: 'token1:nv:read|nv:write,token2:nv:read'). "
129	            "Refusing to expose an unauthenticated control plane."
130	        )
131	    return StaticTokenVerifier(
132	        tokens={
133	            token: {"client_id": f"nv-mcp-{i}", "scopes": scopes}
134	            for i, (token, scopes) in enumerate(settings.http_bearer_tokens.items())
135	        }

139	def build_server(settings: Settings | None = None) -> FastMCP:
140	    """Construct the fully wired :class:`FastMCP` server.
141	
142	    Args:
143	        settings: Injected settings. Tests pass a constructed
144	            :class:`~neuvector_mcp.config.Settings`; production passes ``None``
145	            so the environment is read.
146	
147	    Returns:
148	        A server ready for ``.run()`` or for in-process testing with
149	        ``fastmcp.Client(server)``.
150	    """
151	    settings = settings or load_settings()
152	    configure_logging(settings)
153	
154	    mcp = FastMCP(
155	        name=SERVER_NAME,
156	        version=SERVER_VERSION,
157	        instructions=INSTRUCTIONS,
158	        lifespan=lifespan,
159	        auth=_auth_provider(settings),
160	        middleware=[AuditMiddleware(settings)],
161	        mask_error_details=False,

165	
166	    for module in TOOL_MODULES:

169	    return mcp

171	
172	def main() -> None:

175	    mcp = build_server(settings)
176	    if settings.transport == "http":
177	        mcp.run(
178	            transport="http",
179	            host=settings.http_host,
180	            port=settings.http_port,
181	            path=settings.http_path,
182	            show_banner=False,
183	        )
184	    else:
185	        mcp.run(transport="stdio", show_banner=False)

2	
3	The controller returns errors as a ``RESTError`` JSON body::

5	    {"code": 7, "error": "Object not found", "message": "Group not found"}

8	the HTTP status is chosen per call site. Always branch on ``code`` first and fall
9	back to the HTTP status only when the body is absent or unparseable.

77	class NeuVectorMCPError(ToolError):

118	_CODE_MAP: dict[int, type[NeuVectorMCPError]] = {

120	    ERR_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED: UpstreamError,
121	    ERR_UNAUTHORIZED: AuthError,
122	    ERR_OP_NOT_ALLOWED: PermissionError_,
123	    ERR_TOO_MANY_LOGIN_USER: UpstreamError,
124	    ERR_INVALID_REQUEST: ValidationError_,
125	    ERR_OBJECT_NOT_FOUND: NotFoundError,
126	    ERR_NOT_ENOUGH_FILTER: ValidationError_,

132	    ERR_READ_ONLY_RULES: PermissionError_,

136	    ERR_ADMCTRL_UNSUPPORTED: ValidationError_,
137	    ERR_WORKLOAD_NOT_RUNNING: ConflictError,
138	}

141	_STATUS_MAP: dict[int, type[NeuVectorMCPError]] = {
142	    400: ValidationError_,
143	    401: AuthError,
144	    403: PermissionError_,
145	    404: NotFoundError,
146	    405: UpstreamError,
147	    408: UpstreamError,
148	    409: ConflictError,
149	    413: TooLargeError,
150	    429: UpstreamError,

154	def classify(status_code: int, body: Any) -> NeuVectorMCPError:
155	    """Turn a non-2xx controller response into the right exception instance.
156	
157	    Args:
158	        status_code: HTTP status returned by the controller.
159	        body: Parsed JSON body, or ``None``/``str`` when the body was not JSON.
160	
161	    Returns:
162	        An unraised :class:`NeuVectorMCPError` subclass instance whose message is
163	        safe to hand to a model: it names the controller code, the controller's
164	        own ``error`` string, and its ``message`` detail when present.
165	    """
166	    code: int | None = None
167	    err_str = ""
168	    detail = ""
169	    if isinstance(body, dict):
170	        raw_code = body.get("code")
171	        if isinstance(raw_code, int):
172	            code = raw_code
173	        err_str = str(body.get("error") or "")
174	        detail = str(body.get("message") or "")
175	
176	    cls = _CODE_MAP.get(code) if code is not None else None
177	    if cls is None:
178	        cls = _STATUS_MAP.get(status_code, UpstreamError)
179	
180	    parts = [f"NeuVector controller returned HTTP {status_code}"]
181	    if code is not None:
182	        parts.append(f"code={code}")
183	    if err_str:
184	        parts.append(err_str)
185	    if detail and detail != err_str:
186	        parts.append(detail)
187	    return cls(": ".join(parts[:2]) + (" - " + " / ".join(parts[2:]) if parts[2:] else ""))
188	
189	
190	def is_retryable(status_code: int, body: Any) -> bool:
191	    """True when the failure is transient and a bounded retry is appropriate."""
192	    if status_code in (502, 503, 504):
193	        return True
194	    if isinstance(body, dict):
195	        code = body.get("code")
196	        if isinstance(code, int) and code in RETRYABLE_CODES:
197	            return True
198	    return False

1	"""Structured logging and the tool-call audit middleware.
2	
3	Two responsibilities:
4	
5	* :func:`configure_logging` sets up structlog once, at process start.
6	* :class:`AuditMiddleware` emits one record per ``tools/call`` with the tool
7	  name, argument keys (never values), outcome, duration and error class.
8	
9	Argument *values* are never logged: a caller may pass a registry password or a
10	user password through a mutating tool. Only key names are recorded.
11	"""
12	
13	from __future__ import annotations
14	
15	import logging
16	import sys
17	import time
18	from typing import Any
19	
20	import structlog
21	from fastmcp.server.middleware import CallNext, Middleware, MiddlewareContext
22	
23	from .config import Settings
24	
25	_SENSITIVE_KEYS = {"password", "secret", "token", "confirm", "api_secret_key"}
26	
27	
28	def configure_logging(settings: Settings) -> None:
29	    """Configure structlog for the process. Idempotent.
30	
31	    stdio transport is a hard constraint: **all** logs go to stderr, because
32	    stdout carries the MCP JSON-RPC framing. Writing a single byte of log output
33	    to stdout corrupts the session.
34	    """
35	    logging.basicConfig(
36	        format="%(message)s",
37	        stream=sys.stderr,
38	        level=getattr(logging, settings.log_level, logging.INFO),
39	        force=True,
40	    )
41	    processors: list[Any] = [
42	        structlog.contextvars.merge_contextvars,
43	        structlog.processors.add_log_level,
44	        structlog.processors.TimeStamper(fmt="iso", utc=True),
45	        structlog.processors.StackInfoRenderer(),
46	    ]
47	    if settings.log_format == "json":
48	        processors.append(structlog.processors.JSONRenderer())
49	    else:
50	        processors.append(structlog.dev.ConsoleRenderer(colors=False))
51	    structlog.configure(
52	        processors=processors,
53	        logger_factory=structlog.PrintLoggerFactory(file=sys.stderr),
54	        wrapper_class=structlog.make_filtering_bound_logger(
55	            getattr(logging, settings.log_level, logging.INFO)
56	        ),
57	        cache_logger_on_first_use=True,
58	    )
59	
60	
61	class AuditMiddleware(Middleware):
62	    """Emit one audit record per tool call."""
63	
64	    def __init__(self, settings: Settings) -> None:
65	        self._s = settings
66	        self._log = structlog.get_logger("neuvector_mcp.audit")
67	
68	    async def on_call_tool(
69	        self,
70	        context: MiddlewareContext[Any],
71	        call_next: CallNext[Any, Any],
72	    ) -> Any:
73	        params = getattr(context, "message", None)
74	        tool_name = getattr(params, "name", "<unknown>")
75	        raw_args = getattr(params, "arguments", None) or {}
76	        arg_keys = sorted(raw_args.keys()) if isinstance(raw_args, dict) else []
77	        confirmed = bool(isinstance(raw_args, dict) and raw_args.get("confirm"))
78	        started = time.monotonic()
79	        try:
80	            result = await call_next(context)
81	        except Exception as exc:
82	            self._log.warning(
83	                "tool.call",
84	                tool=tool_name,
85	                arg_keys=arg_keys,
86	                confirmed=confirmed,
87	                outcome="error",
88	                error_class=type(exc).__name__,
89	                error=str(exc)[:400],
90	                duration_ms=round((time.monotonic() - started) * 1000, 1),
91	            )
92	            raise
93	        self._log.info(
94	            "tool.call",
95	            tool=tool_name,
96	            arg_keys=arg_keys,
97	            confirmed=confirmed,
98	            outcome="ok",
99	            duration_ms=round((time.monotonic() - started) * 1000, 1),
100	        )
101	        return result
102	
103	
104	def redact(mapping: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
105	    """Return a copy of ``mapping`` with sensitive values replaced."""
106	    return {
107	        k: ("***REDACTED***" if any(s in k.lower() for s in _SENSITIVE_KEYS) else v)
108	        for k, v in mapping.items()
109	    }

1	"""Enforcement-mode changes on ``PATCH /v1/service/config``.
2	
3	Two things about that endpoint are not in the published API documentation. Both
4	were measured against a live 5.6.0 controller, and getting them wrong is silent
5	in both directions - the controller answers 200 either way.
6	
7	1. **The dimension is chosen by the payload field, not by the path.**
8	   ``RESTServiceBatchConfig`` carries five fields: ``services``, ``policy_mode``,
9	   ``profile_mode``, ``baseline_profile`` and ``not_scored``. Sending
10	   ``profile_mode`` to ``/v1/service/config`` moves the process/file profile and
11	   leaves network policy alone. The sibling route ``/v1/service/config/profile``
12	   is inert on every field; ``/v1/service/config/network`` honours only
13	   ``policy_mode``. This module therefore uses ``/v1/service/config`` alone.
14	
15	2. **The write is applied asynchronously.** A read issued immediately after the
16	   200 can still show the old value. Measured lag on 2026-07-31: 0.33-0.59s over
17	   five runs. :func:`verify_applied` polls across that window, because a single
18	   read taken too early reports a change that succeeded as a failure.
19	
20	An earlier revision of this module also stepped every mode change through
21	``Monitor``, on the theory that the controller silently discards a two-rung move
22	along ``Discover -> Monitor -> Protect``. That theory was wrong: it was point 2
23	misread. Five consecutive single-call ``Discover -> Protect`` moves all landed,
24	on both dimensions, including with the other dimension already at ``Protect``.
25	The stepping is gone; the verification it was hiding behind is what actually
26	mattered and has been kept.
27	
28	The pure functions here decide what to send and what counts as landed; the
29	callers in ``tools`` own the guard handshake and do the sending.
30	"""
31	
32	from __future__ import annotations
33	
34	import asyncio
35	from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
36	from typing import Any
37	
38	from .client import NeuVectorClient, build_query
39	
40	#: Every settable field of ``RESTServiceBatchConfig`` bar ``services``. Each one
41	#: is also a field of ``RESTService``, which is what makes read-back possible.
42	SERVICE_CONFIG_FIELDS: tuple[str, ...] = (
43	    "policy_mode",
44	    "profile_mode",
45	    "baseline_profile",
46	    "not_scored",
47	)
48	
49	#: Read-back budget, sized off the measured 0.33-0.59s propagation lag with room
50	#: for a loaded controller. Module-level so tests can shrink them.
51	VERIFY_ATTEMPTS = 8
52	VERIFY_DELAY_S = 0.5
53	
54	
55	def pending_fields(
56	    services: Sequence[str],
57	    config: Mapping[str, Any],
58	    observed: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, Any]],
59	) -> list[str]:
60	    """Fields of ``config`` that ``observed`` does not already satisfy.
61	
62	    Args:
63	        services: Service names in the batch.
64	        config: The ``config`` object the caller asked for, ``services`` included.
65	        observed: Current field values per service, from :func:`read_service_modes`.
66	
67	    Returns:
68	        One human-readable line per service-and-field still to change. Empty means
69	        the request is a no-op and nothing need be sent.
70	    """
71	    return [
72	        f"{service}.{field}: asked for {value!r}, controller reports "
73	        f"{observed.get(service, {}).get(field)!r}"
74	        for service in services
75	        for field, value in sorted(config.items())
76	        if field != "services" and observed.get(service, {}).get(field) != value
77	    ]
78	
79	
80	async def read_service_modes(
81	    client: NeuVectorClient, services: Sequence[str]
82	) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
83	    """Read the current :data:`SERVICE_CONFIG_FIELDS` of each named service.
84	
85	    One ``GET /v1/service`` per service: the batch endpoint takes a service list
86	    but the read side has no way to ask for several named services at once. The
87	    name filter is a prefix filter, so the exact name is matched again here.
88	
89	    Args:
90	        client: Controller client.
91	        services: Service names, e.g. ``["api.prod"]``.
92	
93	    Returns:
94	        ``{service: {field: value}}``. A service the controller does not know is
95	        absent from the mapping rather than present with empty values.
96	    """
97	    observed: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
98	    for name in services:
99	        params = build_query(start=0, limit=100, filters={"name": f"prefix,{name}"})
100	        items = await client.get_list("/v1/service", "services", params=params)
101	        for item in items:
102	            if isinstance(item, dict) and item.get("name") == name:
103	                observed[name] = {field: item.get(field) for field in SERVICE_CONFIG_FIELDS}
104	                break
105	    return observed
106	
107	
108	async def verify_applied(
109	    client: NeuVectorClient, services: Sequence[str], config: Mapping[str, Any]
110	) -> list[str]:
111	    """Poll the controller until it reflects ``config``, and report what never did.
112	
113	    A 200 from ``PATCH /v1/service/config`` is not evidence, and neither is one
114	    read taken straight after it - the write lands a fraction of a second later.
115	    Returning early on the first clean read keeps the common case fast.
116	
117	    Args:
118	        client: Controller client.
119	        services: Service names in the batch.
120	        config: The ``config`` object that was sent.
121	
122	    Returns:
123	        Empty when everything landed. Otherwise one line per field that did not,
124	        naming the value the controller actually holds.
125	    """
126	    drift: list[str] = []
127	    for attempt in range(VERIFY_ATTEMPTS):
128	        drift = pending_fields(services, config, await read_service_modes(client, services))
129	        if not drift:
130	            return []
131	        if attempt + 1 < VERIFY_ATTEMPTS:
132	            await asyncio.sleep(VERIFY_DELAY_S)
133	    return drift

@mcp.tool(
        name="nv_get_compliance_profile",
        annotations=READ_ONLY,
        tags={"compliance", "read"},
    )
    async def nv_get_compliance_profile(
        ctx: Context,
        profile_name: Annotated[
            str,
            Field(
                min_length=1,
                description="Profile name from nv_list_compliance_profiles. Almost always "
                "'default'.",
            ),
        ] = "default",
        max_entries: Annotated[
            int,
            Field(
                ge=0,
                le=500,
                description="Maximum per-check overrides to return. 0 returns the count only.",
            ),
        ] = 100,
    ) -> ComplianceProfile:
        """One compliance profile with its per-check tag overrides.

        Each entry re-tags a single CIS check with the standards it should count
        towards, e.g. PCI or GDPR, which is what makes a check show up in one
        compliance report and not another. Read this when a check appears under an
        unexpected standard, or when disable_system is set and built-in checks have
        gone missing.

        Calls GET /v1/compliance/profile/{name}.
        """
        app = app_context(ctx)
        # Envelope key "profile" is convention-derived: Appendix B has no
        # RESTComplianceProfileData. A different wrapper yields {} -> NotFoundError,
        # which is preferable to returning wrong data.
        raw = await app.client.get_object(f"/v1/compliance/profile/{profile_name}", "profile")
        if not raw:
            from ..errors import NotFoundError

            raise NotFoundError(f"no compliance profile named {profile_name!r}")
        return ComplianceProfile.from_api(raw, max_entries=min(max_entries, app.settings.max_items))

# Base image policy: openSUSE / SUSE BCI only.
#
# SUSE BCI Python (SLE-based, SUSE-supported lifecycle) is the build and runtime
# base. The openSUSE equivalent, registry.opensuse.org/opensuse/bci/python, is
# the only other permitted base -- but as of 2026-07 its :3.13 manifest list
# publishes no linux/amd64 image (arm, arm64, ppc64le, riscv64 and s390x only),
# so swapping to it breaks the build on x86_64. Its :3.12 tag does carry amd64.
# No base outside those two is permitted here.
#
#   builder : creates a self-contained venv with pinned wheels
#   runtime  : copies the venv, drops privileges, no compilers on the final image

FROM registry.suse.com/bci/python:3.13 AS builder

ENV PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK=1 \
    PIP_NO_CACHE_DIR=1 \
    VIRTUAL_ENV=/opt/venv \
    PATH="/opt/venv/bin:$PATH"

WORKDIR /build
RUN python3 -m venv "$VIRTUAL_ENV"

# Dependency layer first so source edits do not invalidate the wheel cache.
COPY pyproject.toml README.md ./
COPY src ./src
RUN python3 -m pip install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel \
 && python3 -m pip install .

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
FROM registry.suse.com/bci/python:3.13 AS runtime

LABEL org.opencontainers.image.title="neuvector-mcp" \
      org.opencontainers.image.description="MCP server for SUSE NeuVector" \
      org.opencontainers.image.licenses="Apache-2.0" \
      org.opencontainers.image.base.name="registry.suse.com/bci/python:3.13"

ENV VIRTUAL_ENV=/opt/venv \
    PATH="/opt/venv/bin:$PATH" \
    PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
    NV_TRANSPORT=http \
    NV_HTTP_HOST=0.0.0.0 \
    NV_HTTP_PORT=8080 \
    NV_READ_ONLY=true \
    NV_LOG_FORMAT=json

COPY --from=builder /opt/venv /opt/venv

# Fixed uid/gid so a PodSecurity "restricted" namespace can pin runAsUser.
RUN groupadd --gid 10001 nvmcp \
 && useradd  --uid 10001 --gid 10001 --home-dir /home/nvmcp --create-home --shell /sbin/nologin nvmcp \
 && chown -R 10001:10001 /opt/venv

USER 10001:10001
WORKDIR /home/nvmcp
EXPOSE 8080

# The server exposes no HTTP health path of its own; a TCP probe on the MCP port
# is the correct liveness signal. See deploy/deployment.yaml.
ENTRYPOINT ["neuvector-mcp"]

---
# Namespace: deploy alongside NeuVector but not inside it, so a NeuVector
# upgrade never touches this workload.
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: neuvector-mcp
  labels:
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: restricted
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/audit: restricted
---
# Controller credentials. Create the API key in NeuVector first:
#   Settings -> API Keys -> Add, role "reader" for read-only deployments.
# Replace both values, or better: manage this Secret with SOPS / External Secrets
# and never commit plaintext.
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: neuvector-mcp-controller
  namespace: neuvector-mcp
type: Opaque
stringData:
  access-key: REPLACE_ME
  secret-key: REPLACE_ME
---
# Bearer tokens that MCP clients present. Format:
#   <token>:<scope>|<scope>,<token2>:<scope>
# Generate with: openssl rand -hex 32
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: neuvector-mcp-clients
  namespace: neuvector-mcp
type: Opaque
stringData:
  bearer-tokens: "REPLACE_ME_32_BYTE_HEX:nv:read"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: neuvector-mcp-config
  namespace: neuvector-mcp
data:
  NV_CONTROLLER_URL: "https://neuvector-svc-controller-api.cattle-neuvector-system.svc:10443"
  NV_VERIFY_TLS: "false"          # controller serves a self-signed cert by default
  NV_AUTH_MODE: "apikey"
  NV_TRANSPORT: "http"
  NV_HTTP_PATH: "/mcp"
  # Write-capable. Every mutating tool still needs the two-step confirm-token
  # handshake below, which is what makes this safe rather than the read-only flag.
  # Flip NV_READ_ONLY to "true" for a deployment that must never write, and cut
  # NV_TOOLSETS back to the five read toolsets to match.
  NV_READ_ONLY: "false"
  NV_TOOLSETS: "inventory,vulnerability,compliance,events,policy_read,policy_write,scan_ops,runtime_ops"
  NV_REQUIRE_CONFIRM_TOKEN: "true"
  NV_MAX_ITEMS: "200"
  NV_MAX_RESPONSE_CHARS: "60000"
  NV_LOG_LEVEL: "INFO"
  NV_LOG_FORMAT: "json"
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: neuvector-mcp
  namespace: neuvector-mcp
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: neuvector-mcp
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: neuvector-mcp
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: neuvector-mcp
    spec:
      automountServiceAccountToken: false
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        runAsUser: 10001
        runAsGroup: 10001
        seccompProfile:
          type: RuntimeDefault
      containers:
        - name: server
          # Built in-cluster by deploy/build-job.yaml, which clones main from
          # GitHub and pushes here. Bump both together.
          image: registry.ash4d.com/ash4d-lab/neuvector-mcp:1.1.2
          imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
          envFrom:
            - configMapRef:
                name: neuvector-mcp-config
          env:
            - name: NV_API_ACCESS_KEY
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: neuvector-mcp-controller
                  key: access-key
            - name: NV_API_SECRET_KEY
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: neuvector-mcp-controller
                  key: secret-key

from __future__ import annotations

import httpx
import pytest
import respx
from conftest import CONTROLLER, make_settings
from fastmcp import Client

@pytest.fixture
def mock_nv() -> respx.MockRouter:
    with respx.mock(base_url=CONTROLLER, assert_all_called=False) as router:
        router.get("/v1/system/summary").respond(200, json={"summary": {}})
        yield router


async def test_read_only_server_reaches_an_unregistered_get_endpoint(mock_nv):
    """A read-only server, compliance toolset only, walks out to GET /v1/user."""
    users = mock_nv.get("/v1/user").respond(200, json={"users": [{"fullname": "admin"}]})
    settings = make_settings(read_only=True, toolsets=("compliance",))
    async with Client(build_server(settings)) as c:
        with pytest.raises(Exception):
            # NotFoundError is expected: the envelope key "profile" is absent.
            await c.call_tool(
                "nv_get_compliance_profile",
                {"profile_name": "../../../v1/user"},
            )
    assert users.called, "traversal did NOT reach /v1/user"
    print("\nREACHED:", str(users.calls[0].request.url))


async def test_namespace_allowlist_escaped_by_group_name(mock_nv):
    """NV_ALLOWED_NAMESPACES=('dev',) still lets a PATCH land on a prod group."""
    patched = mock_nv.patch(path__startswith="/v1/process_profile").respond(200, json={})
    settings = make_settings(
        read_only=False,
        toolsets=("policy_write",),
        allowed_namespaces=("dev",),
        require_confirm_token=False,
    )

    settings = make_settings(

async def test_confirm_token_survives_a_traversing_target(mock_nv):

class StaticTokenVerifier(TokenVerifier):
    """
    Simple static token verifier for testing and development.

    This verifier validates tokens against a predefined dictionary of valid token
    strings and their associated claims. When a token string matches a key in the
    dictionary, the verifier returns the corresponding claims as if the token was
    validated by a real authorization server.

    Use this when:
    - You're developing or testing locally without a real OAuth server
    - You need predictable tokens for automated testing
    - You want to simulate different users/scopes without complex setup
    - You're prototyping and need simple API key-style authentication

    WARNING: Never use this in production - tokens are stored in plain text!
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        tokens: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
        required_scopes: list[str] | None = None,
    ):
        """
        Initialize the static token verifier.

        Args:
            tokens: Dict mapping token strings to token metadata
                   Each token should have: client_id, scopes, expires_at (optional)
            required_scopes: Required scopes for all tokens
        """
        super().__init__(required_scopes=required_scopes)
        self.tokens = tokens

    async def verify_token(self, token: str) -> AccessToken | None:
        """Verify token against static token dictionary."""
        token_data = self.tokens.get(token)
        if not token_data:
            return None

        # Check expiration if present
        expires_at = token_data.get("expires_at")
        if expires_at is not None and expires_at < time.time():
            return None

        scopes = token_data.get("scopes", [])

        # Check required scopes
        if self.required_scopes:
            token_scopes = set(scopes)
            required_scopes = set(self.required_scopes)
            if not required_scopes.issubset(token_scopes):
                logger.debug(
                    f"Token missing required scopes. Has: {token_scopes}, Required: {required_scopes}"
                )
                return None

        return AccessToken(
            token=token,
            client_id=token_data["client_id"],
            scopes=scopes,
            expires_at=expires_at,
            claims=token_data,
        )

"""PoC: an nv:read bearer token can invoke mutating tools over HTTP."""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import contextlib
import threading

import httpx
import respx
import uvicorn
from conftest import CONTROLLER, make_settings
from fastmcp import Client
from fastmcp.client.transports import StreamableHttpTransport

from neuvector_mcp.server import build_server

READ_TOKEN = "aaaa1111bbbb2222"


async def main() -> None:
    settings = make_settings(
        transport="http",
        http_host="127.0.0.1",
        http_port=8399,
        http_bearer_tokens={READ_TOKEN: ["nv:read"]},
        read_only=False,
        toolsets=("policy_write",),
        require_confirm_token=False,
    )
    with respx.mock(base_url=CONTROLLER, assert_all_called=False) as r:
        r.get("/v1/system/summary").respond(200, json={"summary": {}})
        deleted = r.delete(path__startswith="/v1/group").respond(200, json={})

        mcp = build_server(settings)
        app = mcp.http_app(path="/mcp")
        config = uvicorn.Config(app, host="127.0.0.1", port=8399, log_level="error")
        server = uvicorn.Server(config)
        task = asyncio.create_task(server.serve())
        while not server.started:
            await asyncio.sleep(0.05)

        # 1. no token at all
        async with httpx.AsyncClient() as h:
            resp = await h.post(
                "http://127.0.0.1:8399/mcp",
                json={"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "tools/list"},
                headers={"Accept": "application/json, text/event-stream"},
            )
            print(f"no token          -> HTTP {resp.status_code}")

        # 2. nv:read token calling a MUTATING tool
        transport = StreamableHttpTransport(
            "http://127.0.0.1:8399/mcp", headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {READ_TOKEN}"}
        )
        async with Client(transport) as c:
            tools = [t.name for t in await c.list_tools()]
            print(f"nv:read token     -> tools/list OK, {len(tools)} tools visible")
            result = await c.call_tool("nv_delete_group", {"group_name": "some-group"})
            print(f"nv:read token     -> nv_delete_group status={result.data.status}")
        print(f"controller DELETE sent: {deleted.called} "
              f"({deleted.calls[0].request.url if deleted.called else '-'})")

        server.should_exit = True
        with contextlib.suppress(asyncio.CancelledError):
            await task


asyncio.run(main())

content.text:
Audit complete. The engineering gate is genuinely green — ruff, `ruff format`, mypy strict, 647 tests, 97.6% coverage, 9/9 spec rules — so everything below is a real gap the gate does not test for. Every finding was reproduced against the code, not inferred; PoCs are in the scratchpad and nothing in the repo was modified.

## Headline

Three of the four safety controls this server advertises are weaker than documented, and one is inert.

| Control | Advertised | Actual |
|---|---|---|
| Confirm-token handshake | Blocks accidental writes | Works as designed ✅ |
| `NV_READ_ONLY` / toolsets | Registration-time gate | Works, but bypassable via S2 |
| Bearer scopes `nv:read`/`nv:write` | Per-token privilege | **Never checked** |
| `NV_ALLOWED_NAMESPACES` | "mutations outside this list are refused" | Fail-open; 17 of 67 call sites |

---

## Security

**S1 — Bearer token scopes are decorative. (High)**
`config.py:211` parses them, `server.py:133` hands them to `StaticTokenVerifier`, and nothing ever reads them. No tool declares required scopes; `required_scopes` is never set. Verified over real HTTP against the shipped config shape:

```
no token       -> HTTP 401              (auth itself works)
nv:read token  -> tools/list OK, 23 tools visible
nv:read token  -> nv_delete_group status=applied
controller DELETE sent: https://.../v1/group/some-group
```

`deploy/deployment.yaml` ships `bearer-tokens: "REPLACE_ME_32_BYTE_HEX:nv:read"` alongside `NV_READ_ONLY: "false"` and `policy_write,scan_ops,runtime_ops`. An operator following the README gets a token they believe is read-only and which can delete every network rule in the cluster.

**S2 — Path traversal in 63 endpoint paths. (High)**
Every tool builds its path as `f"/v1/group/{group_name}"` with no encoding. httpx normalises `..` before sending:

```
'../../v1/system/config' -> https://ctl:10443/v1/system/config
'a?x=1'                  -> https://ctl:10443/v1/group/a?x=1
```

Verified consequences:
- A **read-only** server with only the `compliance` toolset enabled reached `GET /v1/user` via `nv_get_compliance_profile(profile_name="../../../v1/user")`. The read-only flag and the toolset gate both confine tool *registration*, not reachable *endpoints* — so the credential's full GET surface is available regardless.
- `nv_delete_group("../api_key/mcp-writer")` issued `DELETE /v1/api_key/mcp-writer`. The confirm handshake authorised it happily: the token is derived from the raw string, so it matched.

Fix is one line at the call boundary — `urllib.parse.quote(value, safe="")` on every interpolated segment, ideally centralised in `client.request`.

**S3 — `NV_ALLOWED_NAMESPACES` is fail-open and mostly unwired. (Medium-High)**
`guard.py:90` reads `if namespace and settings.allowed_namespaces and ...` — a `None` namespace skips the check entirely. Across the 67 `authorise_write` call sites, **17 pass a real namespace and 50 pass `None`** (14 omit the kwarg outright). Verified escapes:

- `nv_update_process_profile(group_name="custom-prod-group")` with `allowed_namespaces=("dev",)` → `PATCH` landed. Any group name not starting with `nv.` yields `None`.
- `nv_delete_group("nv.api.prod")` with the same allowlist → `DELETE` landed. This one is an outright inconsistency, not a design limit: `_namespace_from_group_name` exists and is used at `policy_write.py:922/1060/1415`, but `nv_delete_group` at line 285 doesn't call it.

The README's "mutations targeting a namespace outside this list are refused" overstates a control that covers a quarter of the write surface.

**S4 — `StaticTokenVerifier` in production. (Medium)** FastMCP's own docstring: *"WARNING: Never use this in production - tokens are stored in plain text!"* No `expires_at` is set, so tokens never expire; there is no rotation path, no rate limit, and no lockout on the HTTP transport.

**S5 — NetworkPolicy ingress is open. (Medium)** `deployment.yaml` ingress is `- ports: [{port: 8080}]` with no `from:`. An empty peer list permits every pod in every namespace. The comment above it reads "Egress to the controller and DNS only. Nothing else, in or out."

**S6 — `NV_AUDIT_LOG_PATH` is documented but not implemented. (Medium)** README line 212 promises "Optional second sink for audit records." The setting is parsed, validated, and never read. `AuditMiddleware` writes to stderr only, and the container has no persistent sink — with `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true` and an `emptyDir` `/tmp`, the audit trail dies with the pod. `audit.redact()` and `Settings.redacted()` are both dead code (tests only).

**S7 — `NV_VERIFY_TLS: "false"` in the deployed ConfigMap.** A documented tradeoff against the self-signed controller cert, but combined with S5 the controller path is unauthenticated-to-the-server in both directions.

---

## Performance

**P1 — Non-idempotent writes are retried. (High, also a correctness issue)**
`client.request` wraps every method in the same 3-attempt loop, and `is_retryable` returns true for 502/503/504 plus `ERR_FAIL_WRITE_CLUSTER` (code 8). Verified: a `POST /v1/group` failing with code 8 was sent **3 times**. Code 8 is "failed to write to cluster" — a state where the write may have partially landed. A 502 from an ingress in front of the controller has the same shape. Retries should be gated on `method in ("GET",)` unless the tool opts in.

**P2 — Re-login stampede. (Medium)** `client.py:255` acquires `_login_lock` then unconditionally calls `login()` — no double-check that another coroutine already refreshed the token. Verified with a realistic 50 ms login: **10 concurrent requests hitting one expired session issued 10 `POST /v1/auth`**, serialised. NeuVector has `ERR_TOO_MANY_LOGIN_USER` (code 5), so this can lock the identity out during the exact burst it's trying to recover from. Fix is three lines: snapshot `self._token` before the lock, compare after.

**P3 — `verify_applied` scales badly. (Medium)** `modes.py` does one `GET /v1/service` per service (`read_service_modes`), inside a poll loop of `VERIFY_ATTEMPTS=8` × `VERIFY_DELAY_S=0.5`. A 20-service batch worst case is 160 sequential round trips plus 3.5 s of sleeps. The whole codebase uses zero `asyncio.gather` — these are the only three awaits-in-loops in `src/`, and this one is the one worth parallelising.

**P5 — Cold start:** 611 ms to import `neuvector_mcp.server`, 228 ms to build 119 tools. Irrelevant in-cluster; noticeable for a desktop stdio client.

---

## Code quality

The gate is real and it passes — that's worth stating plainly, because most of what follows is minor by comparison.

- **Q2 (Medium)** — `NV_MAX_RESPONSE_CHARS` is documented as "Truncation budget per tool result. Truncated results set `truncated=true`." It is referenced in exactly one place: `events.py:290`, clipping threat packet payloads. Per-result truncation elsewhere is driven by `max_items`. Same class of doc/impl gap as S6.
- **Q3 (Low)** — `build_query` rejects any filter value containing a comma. Verified: `{"name": "team,alpha"}` raises *"filter 'name' uses unknown operator 'team'"*. Needs an explicit op-prefix convention or a `("op", "value")` tuple.
- **Q4 (Low)** — Nine copies of the `READ_ONLY`/`MUTATING` `ToolAnnotations` blocks and three copies of `_namespace_from_group_name`. Spec rule N3 pins one of those copies, so this is partly deliberate. `models.py` at 4053 lines is generated from `build-plan/models-fragments/` and reads like it.
- **Q5 (Low)** — 15 function-level imports in `src/`, mostly `from ..errors import NotFoundError` inside tool bodies, against module-level style everywhere else.
- **Q7 (Low)** — `getattr(logging, settings.log_level, logging.INFO)` is unvalidated; `NV_LOG_LEVEL=raiseExceptions` resolves to `True` → level 1.
- **Q6 (Trivial)** — `.coverage 2` is untracked and `.gitignore`'s `.coverage` doesn't match it.

---

## What I'd fix first

1. **S2** — one `quote()` at the client boundary closes the largest hole and is the cheapest change here.
2. **S1** — either enforce scopes (`required_scopes` per tool via FastMCP, or a middleware check against `nv:write`) or strip them from config and docs. Shipping a control that doesn't exist is worse than not having it.
3. **P1** — restrict the retry loop to GET.
4. **S3** — at minimum, wire `_namespace_from_group_name` into `nv_delete_group`, and change the README to describe the control as it behaves.
5. **S6/Q2** — implement or delete `NV_AUDIT_LOG_PATH` and correct the `NV_MAX_RESPONSE_CHARS` description.

Want me to open issues for these, or start on the S2 fix?
Go ahead and get started

Receipt: starting on S2 — the path-traversal fix — as a complete unit: encode at the interpolation sites, add a backstop in the client, tests for both, gate green. No commits.

Two things to check before I write anything: what SPEC rule N3 pins as verbatim (it covers `client.py`, where I want the backstop), and your git conventions.

=== infra.md ===
# Infrastructure preferences — Rick Ashford

Read by any skill that provisions, containerises, scripts, or deploys.

Companion files: `lab.md` (ash4d lab conventions and repo rules), `working.md`
(how to interact and what counts as verified).

## Containers

- **Images we author default to SUSE / openSUSE BCI base images.** Any
  deviation needs a stated justification and my authorisation before
  proceeding. Example of the rule applied correctly: `dli-power-mcp` builds on
  `registry.suse.com/bci/python`.
- **Pulling a maintained upstream image is not a deviation.** cloudflared,
  nut_exporter and similar vendor-maintained images get used directly — no
  flag, no authorisation request. The policy exists to keep our own build
  artifacts on a supported base, so wrapping someone else's binary in a BCI
  image to satisfy the letter of the rule buys nothing and creates a build path
  to own.

## Configuration management

**Salt is the preferred method for system administration.** A change that can be
expressed as a salt state should be, rather than a one-off SSH command or a
shell script copied to each host. Master is `pecan`; states and pillar live in
the `ash4d-salt` repo.

- **Salt owns the hosts.** Packages, files, services, users, OS-level config.
- **Fleet and `kubectl` own cluster workloads.** Salt manages the machine k3s
  runs on; Fleet manages what runs inside k3s. Keep that line — a salt state
  that applies a manifest puts two systems in charge of the same object.
- Prefer `state.apply` over `cmd.run`. `cmd.run` is permitted and deliberate —
  arbitrary execution at my request is the point of the open eauth ACL — but a
  change worth making twice belongs in a state file.
- Run `state.apply test=True` and show me the diff before applying. `state_verbose`
  is off, so a converged host prints nothing; output means drift, and the diff
  is the interesting part.
- Long operations go through the async API and poll the job. A synchronous call
  blocks until every minion returns and will time out on a real highstate.
- Every job is recorded in the master job cache with user, target, function and
  arguments. That record is the audit trail. Do not SSH to a host to do
  something salt could have done — it bypasses the record.
- Minion layout is not uniform. Package names, config paths and service names
  differ between stock `salt-minion` and the Uyuni Salt Bundle; branch on the
  `saltpath` grain rather than `os_family`. Which host runs which is state —
  it lives in Claude memory, not here.

## Languages

- **Python and Bash** for tooling, automation, harnesses and pipelines.
- Assume competence in Linux and Kubernetes; skip the primer and give me the
  command.

## Git

### Writing into a repo

- **Never Write or Edit into a repo containing `.entire/` from a Cowork
  session.** This covers new files, not only edits, and applies whether or not
  a commit follows. Check before *writing* — checking at commit time is the
  wrong gate and has already let bad writes through.
- Why: entire.io captures agent work through hooks
  (`.claude/settings.json`, `.codex/hooks.json`, `.cursor/hooks.json`). Cowork
  does not run those hooks, so anything Cowork writes into the repo lands with
  no checkpoint lineage and the repo's provenance breaks silently.
- Instead: stage the artifacts to the session scratch dir or the mounted
  `_portfolio` folder, then hand me the file list and intended destination
  paths so I can run it through Claude Code in one step. If something genuinely
  must land immediately — a live incident — say so and get explicit
  authorisation first.
- Applying manifests to a cluster with `kubectl` is fine. It is repo *files*
  that are gated.
- Known entire-tracked repos are listed in `lab.md`.

### Committing

- Before any commit, verify `.entire/settings.json` exists and is correct. If
  it is missing, stop and tell me — do not commit. Never claim entire.io is
  enabled; it can only be verified, not enabled by you.
- Repositories that sync to **darthzen**: leave `.entire/settings.json` and the
  agent hook files committed, and let `entire/checkpoints/v1` push normally.
- Repositories that sync anywhere else: before the first commit, verify entire
  is configured with either `--skip-push-sessions` or
  `--checkpoint-remote github:darthzen/<repo>-checkpoints`. The
  `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch must never reach a remote I do not own. Do not
  stage `.entire/` or agent hook files into a pull request against that repo —
  use `entire enable --local` so the config stays in `settings.local.json`,
  which is gitignored.
- Commit only on my explicit instruction. I handle git.

## Secrets

- Credentials live in `~/Developer/keys/<service>/`, never in a doc, a
  preferences file, or a repo.
- Do not copy a token, key, or PAT into any file you create, including files in
  this folder. Reference where it lives instead.

## Working in a sandbox

- A sandboxed shell may be able to create files under `.git/` but not delete
  them, which strands `index.lock` and blocks every later git command. If a
  delete fails with "Operation not permitted", request delete permission for
  the folder rather than leaving the lock in place.
- Cloud-synced folders (iCloud, Dropbox) may hold files that exist only in the
  cloud. A shell command will error on those; reading the file downloads it
  first.
- The sandboxed shell and the file tools do not share a filesystem. Paths under
  the Claude application-support tree — memory files among them — are reachable
  by the file tools only.

#: Characters permitted in an assembled controller path. Every tool builds its
#: path by interpolating a caller-supplied object name into an f-string, e.g.
#: ``f"/v1/group/{group_name}"``. This is the unreserved set plus the sub-delims
#: and ``%``, and deliberately excludes ``?``, ``#``, backslash, whitespace and
#: control characters -- the delimiters that let a name change which endpoint,
#: or which query, the request lands on.
_SAFE_PATH = re.compile(r"^/v[12]/[A-Za-z0-9._~!$&'()*+,;=:@%/-]*$")


def validate_path(path: str) -> str:
    """Refuse a controller path that escapes the endpoint the tool named.

    ``httpx`` resolves ``..`` against the base URL before the request goes out,
    so an unvalidated object name is an endpoint selector::

        f"/v1/group/{group_name}" with group_name="../../v1/system/config"
        -> https://controller:10443/v1/system/config

    That defeats both the read-only flag and ``NV_TOOLSETS``, which gate which
    *tools* exist rather than which *endpoints* are reachable. It also defeats
    ``NV_ALLOWED_NAMESPACES``, and the confirmation token is derived from the
    same unvalidated string, so the handshake authorises the escape.

    Percent-encoded traversal is rejected too: ``httpx`` forwards ``%2e%2e``
    untouched and the controller is the one that decodes it, so the check runs
    against both the literal path and its decoded form.

    Args:
        path: The assembled path, e.g. ``"/v1/group/nv.api.prod"``.

    Returns:
        ``path`` unchanged. Legitimate names -- including the dots in
        ``nv.api.prod``, the colon in ``sha256:aaa111`` and the slash in a
        repository like ``library/api`` -- pass through byte-for-byte.

    Raises:
        ValidationError_: if the path is malformed or contains a traversal
            segment. Nothing is sent to the controller.
    """
    if not _SAFE_PATH.match(path):
        raise ValidationError_(
            f"refusing to send controller path {path!r}: it is not a well-formed "
            "/v1 or /v2 path, or an argument contained a URL delimiter such as "
            "'?', '#' or whitespace. Nothing was sent to the controller."
        )
    for candidate in (path, unquote(path)):
        if any(segment in ("..", ".") for segment in candidate.split("/")):
            raise ValidationError_(
                f"refusing to send controller path {path!r}: an argument contains a "
                "path traversal segment, which would redirect this call to a "
                "different controller endpoint. Nothing was sent to the controller."
            )
    return path
