"""Path-safety contract: a caller-supplied name may not choose the endpoint.

Every tool builds its controller path by interpolating an argument into an
f-string, e.g. ``f"/v1/group/{group_name}"``. Unvalidated, that argument is an
endpoint selector rather than an object name, because ``httpx`` resolves ``..``
against the base URL before the request goes out::

    group_name="../../v1/system/config"
    -> DELETE https://controller:10443/v1/system/config

That escapes three of this server's four safety controls at once: ``NV_READ_ONLY``
and ``NV_TOOLSETS`` gate which *tools* are registered rather than which
*endpoints* are reachable, ``NV_ALLOWED_NAMESPACES`` never sees the real target,
and the confirmation token is derived from the same unvalidated string, so the
handshake authorises the escape.

These tests pin the refusal, pin that nothing reaches the controller when it
fires, and pin that legitimate names still pass through byte-for-byte.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

import pytest
import respx
from conftest import CONTROLLER, fixture, make_settings
from fastmcp import Client

from neuvector_mcp.client import validate_path
from neuvector_mcp.errors import NeuVectorMCPError, ValidationError_
from neuvector_mcp.server import build_server

# Names the controller genuinely uses. None of these may be rejected: dots in a
# learned group name, a colon in an image digest, a slash in a repository path,
# and the percent that survives an already-encoded segment.
LEGITIMATE = [
    "/v1/system/summary",
    "/v1/group/nv.api.prod",
    "/v1/group/custom-group_1",
    "/v1/scan/image/sha256:aaa111",
    "/v1/scan/registry/harbor/image/library/api:1.4.2",
    "/v1/user/admin@example.com/role/reader",
    "/v2/scan/registry/my-registry",
    "/v1/compliance/profile/default/entry/D.1.1.1",
    "/v1/group/a%20name",
]

# Every one of these changes which endpoint the request lands on.
MALICIOUS = [
    "/v1/group/../../v1/system/config",
    "/v1/group/../api_key/mcp-writer",
    "/v1/compliance/profile/../../../v1/user",
    "/v1/group/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/v1/system/config",
    "/v1/group/..%2f..%2fv1%2fsystem%2fconfig",
    "/v1/group/./config",
    "/v1/group/name?f_domain=prod",
    "/v1/group/name#fragment",
    "/v1/group/name with space",
    "/v1/group/back\\slash",
    "/v1/group/nul\x00byte",
    "/etc/passwd",
    "/v3/group/name",
    "v1/group/name",
]


# --- unit ---------------------------------------------------------------------


@pytest.mark.parametrize("path", LEGITIMATE)
def test_legitimate_paths_pass_through_unchanged(path: str) -> None:
    assert validate_path(path) == path


@pytest.mark.parametrize("path", MALICIOUS)
def test_traversal_and_delimiter_injection_are_refused(path: str) -> None:
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError_):
        validate_path(path)


def test_refusal_is_a_tool_error_so_the_model_sees_it() -> None:
    """ValidationError_ is a ToolError subclass; a raw exception would 500."""
    assert issubclass(ValidationError_, NeuVectorMCPError)


# --- integration: nothing reaches the controller ------------------------------


async def test_read_only_server_cannot_walk_out_to_another_get_endpoint(
    nv_mock: respx.MockRouter,
) -> None:
    """A read-only server with one read toolset stays inside that toolset's routes.

    Before validation this reached GET /v1/user, because read_only and toolsets
    gate registration and not reachability.
    """
    users = nv_mock.get("/v1/user").respond(200, json={"users": []})
    server = build_server(make_settings(read_only=True, toolsets=("compliance",)))
    async with Client(server) as c:
        with pytest.raises(Exception, match="traversal"):
            await c.call_tool(
                "nv_get_compliance_profile", {"profile_name": "../../../v1/user"}
            )
    assert not users.called, "traversal still reached /v1/user"


async def test_traversing_delete_sends_nothing(client: Any, nv_mock: respx.MockRouter) -> None:
    """The escape is refused even once the confirmation handshake has authorised it."""
    everything = nv_mock.route(method="DELETE").respond(200, json={})
    evil = "../api_key/mcp-writer"

    plan = await client.call_tool("nv_delete_group", {"group_name": evil})
    assert plan.data.status == "confirmation_required"
    assert not everything.called, "the preview call must never send a request"

    with pytest.raises(Exception, match="traversal"):
        await client.call_tool(
            "nv_delete_group", {"group_name": evil, "confirm": plan.data.confirm_token}
        )
    assert not everything.called, "confirmed traversal still reached the controller"


async def test_query_injection_through_a_name_sends_nothing(
    client: Any, nv_mock: respx.MockRouter
) -> None:
    everything = nv_mock.route().respond(200, json={})
    with pytest.raises(Exception, match="URL delimiter"):
        await client.call_tool("nv_get_process_profile", {"group_name": "nv.api.prod?scope=fed"})
    assert not everything.called


# --- integration: legitimate calls are untouched ------------------------------


async def test_a_real_group_name_still_reaches_the_real_route(
    client: Any, nv_mock: respx.MockRouter
) -> None:
    route = nv_mock.get("/v1/process_profile/nv.api.prod").respond(
        200, json=fixture("process_profile")
    )
    await client.call_tool("nv_get_process_profile", {"group_name": "nv.api.prod"})
    assert route.called
    assert str(route.calls[0].request.url) == f"{CONTROLLER}/v1/process_profile/nv.api.prod"

content.text:
S2 is fixed, verified, and the full gate is green. No commit — your tree, your call.

## What changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/neuvector_mcp/client.py` | +76 lines: `validate_path()` plus one call in `request()` |
| `tests/test_path_safety.py` | New, 28 tests |

The fix is central rather than per-site: `client.request()` refuses any assembled path that isn't a well-formed `/v1`/`/v2` path, contains a `..` or `.` segment (checked against both the literal string and its percent-decoded form), or carries a URL delimiter — `?`, `#`, backslash, whitespace, control chars. One file, no risk of a botched edit across 63 f-strings.

## Verification

Re-ran the original exploit PoCs against the patched tree. The split is exactly right:

```
FAILED  test_read_only_server_reaches_an_unregistered_get_endpoint   <- S2 dead
FAILED  test_confirm_token_survives_a_traversing_target              <- S2 dead
passed  test_namespace_allowlist_escaped_by_group_name               <- S3, untouched
passed  test_delete_group_ignores_namespace_allowlist                <- S3, untouched
passed  test_failed_write_is_retried_three_times                     <- P1, untouched
```

Gate: `ruff` clean · `ruff format` clean · `mypy --strict` clean · **674 passed, 1 xfailed** · coverage **97.64%** · spec **9/9**.

## Two things I decided, so you can overrule them

- **`/` is still permitted in a name**, because a registry image id genuinely is a repository path (`.../image/library/api:1.4.2`). The residual is route confusion — `nv_delete_registry("reg/scan")` hits `DELETE /v1/scan/registry/reg/scan` instead of `.../reg`. It cannot escalate, since reaching a higher-privilege route means going *up*, which needs `..`. Documented in the `validate_path` docstring rather than fixed.
- **SPEC N3 says `client.py` is verbatim from `reference/`.** It isn't gate-enforced, and `client.py`, `config.py` and `guard.py` had already drifted. I changed `src/` and left `neuvector-mcp-spec/reference/` alone.

## Next

P1 (retry non-idempotent writes) and S3 (namespace allowlist) I can just do — both have a single correct answer. S1 doesn't:

content.text:
Your principle is clear; the ambiguity is which direction it points. Let me not guess on a security control that changes live behaviour.

Reading it as: **the token carries the privilege, and it gets checked in exactly one place** — not as per-tool checks scattered through 67 write bodies, and not as a fifth independent gate alongside `NV_READ_ONLY`, `NV_TOOLSETS`, the confirm handshake and `NV_ALLOWED_NAMESPACES`.

That has a clean single-choke-point implementation, because the data already exists: gate rule R3 guarantees every tool's `readOnlyHint` is derived from its toolset. So one middleware reads the caller's token scopes and the tool's own `readOnlyHint`, and refuses a mutating call without `nv:write`. No per-tool code, no new tool→scope map, one function to breakpoint when it misbehaves.

The other reading of your answer is that scopes shouldn't exist at all — privilege comes from the NeuVector API key's role, and our bearer token is just a credential.

questions.question: Which did you mean — enforce the token's scope at one choke point, or drop the scope concept?

options.label: One choke point, token decides
options.description: Add a single middleware next to AuditMiddleware: reads the token's scopes and the tool's readOnlyHint (already guaranteed correct by gate rule R3), refuses a mutating tool without nv:write. Nothing changes in any tool body. Live impact: your deployed nv:read token stops being able to write on the next rollout — it would need nv:read|nv:write in the neuvector-mcp-clients Secret.

options.label: Drop the scope concept
options.description: Scope comes from the NeuVector API key's own role instead; the bearer token is just a credential. Remove parsing from config.py, the format from the README, and the suffix from deploy/deployment.yaml. No behaviour change on the running cluster.

HTTP is network-reachable, so it **must** be authenticated. The server refuses
to start on `NV_TRANSPORT=http` without at least one bearer token in

## ⚠️ Deploy blocker

Your live `Secret/neuvector-mcp-clients` holds a token with a `:nv:read` suffix. That suffix is now a **startup error**, so the pod will CrashLoopBackOff on the next rollout until the Secret carries a bare token:

```bash
kubectl -n neuvector-mcp create secret generic neuvector-mcp-clients \
  --from-literal=bearer-tokens="$(kubectl -n neuvector-mcp get secret neuvector-mcp-clients \
     -o jsonpath='{.data.bearer-tokens}' | base64 -d | cut -d: -f1)" \
  --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
```

I chose loud over silent deliberately: stripping the suffix quietly would preserve your belief in a control that never existed, and keeping it would make the whole string the token and 401 every request.

| Finding | Fix | Verified by |
|---|---|---|
| **S2** path traversal | `validate_path()` in `client.request` | 28 new tests; both original exploits now fail |
| **S1** decorative scopes | Scope concept removed from `config.py`, `server.py`, README, `deployment.yaml` | Live HTTP: 401 without a token, plain token works; suffixed token refused at startup |
| **S9** *(new)* | `load_settings` re-raises with inputs stripped | 5 new tests across every rejection route |

**S9 was not in the audit — I found it while writing the S1 test.** Any `Settings` validation failure rendered pydantic's `input_value`, which is the whole settings dict, so a typo'd `NV_TOOLSETS` printed `NV_API_SECRET_KEY` and `NV_PASSWORD` to stderr → pod log → log shipper. # Handoff

Capture everything a fresh session needs to continue this work, so the current
session can be ended without losing ground.

**Why this exists.** Every turn re-reads the entire accumulated prefix, so cost
per turn climbs with session length — measured at ~26K cache-read tokens per
turn in short sessions versus ~109K past 100 turns. Ending a long session at a
clean boundary and restarting with a handoff is the largest available
efficiency lever. The handoff is what makes ending cheap.

## Where to write it

```
~/.claude/handoffs/<cwd-with-slashes-as-dashes>.md
```

For example, `/Users/rashford/Developer/kitsune` →
`~/.claude/handoffs/-Users-rashford-Developer-kitsune.md`

Overwrite any existing file for this directory — the newest handoff wins. The
`SessionStart` hook loads it automatically in the next session, so **do not**
paste the contents back into chat.

## What to write

Aim for something a competent stranger could act on. Be concrete: real paths,
real command names, real decisions. Skip anything reconstructible from the repo
or from `git log` — those are already available to the next session.

```markdown
# Handoff — <one-line description of the work>
Written: <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM> · Session: <turns> turns

## Where things stand
Two or three sentences. What was being worked on and what state it is in
right now — not a history of the session.

## Decisions made (and why)
Only decisions that would otherwise be re-litigated. Include the reasoning,
because the reasoning is the part that gets lost.

## Files touched
- `path/to/file` — what changed and why

## What's verified vs assumed
Explicit. If tests ran, say so and give the result. If something was assumed
and never checked, say that too — this is the section that prevents the next
session from building on sand.

## Next step
The single next action, stated concretely. Then anything queued behind it.

## Open questions
Things the user needs to decide, or that were left unresolved.
```

## Procedure

1. **Write the file.** Use the path convention above. Do not ask where to put it.
2. **Confirm briefly** — one line naming the file and the next step it records.
3. **Tell the user to `/clear`** (or start a new session). Do not run `/clear`
   yourself; it is theirs to trigger.

## Notes

- Leave out anything sensitive — the handoff is plain text on disk.
- Handoffs older than 14 days are ignored by the loader.
- To skip loading a handoff for one session, start with `HANDOFF_DISABLE=1`.
- If the user asks for a handoff without wanting to stop, write it anyway and
  skip the `/clear` suggestion.

Working tree is dirty on `main`, nothing committed (Rick handles git). Full gate
is green: `ruff`, `ruff format`, `mypy --strict`, **680 passed / 1 xfailed**,
coverage **97.65%**, `verify_spec.py` 9/9.

**There is a deploy blocker.** See "Next step".

## The audit findings (the working list)

Fixed:
- **S2 (High) — path traversal.** All 63 tool endpoint paths are f-strings with
  unencoded arguments. httpx resolves `..` against the base URL, so an argument
  selected the endpoint. Proven: a read-only server with only the `compliance`
  toolset reached `GET /v1/user`; `nv_delete_group("../api_key/mcp-writer")`
  issued `DELETE /v1/api_key/mcp-writer` and the confirm handshake authorised it.
- **S1 (High) — bearer scopes were decorative.** `nv:read`/`nv:write` were parsed
  in `config.py`, handed to `StaticTokenVerifier`, never read. Proven over real
  HTTP: an `nv:read` token called `nv_delete_group` and the DELETE landed.
- **S9 (High, found mid-fix, not in the original audit)** — any `Settings`
  validation failure rendered pydantic's `input_value`, i.e. the whole settings
  dict, so a typo'd `NV_TOOLSETS` printed `NV_API_SECRET_KEY`/`NV_PASSWORD` to
  stderr → pod log → log shipper. Direct SPEC N8 violation.

Still open, in the order agreed:
- **P1 (High, correctness)** — `client.request` retries every method 3× when
  `is_retryable` says so, including `ERR_FAIL_WRITE_CLUSTER` (code 8) and
  502/504. Proven: a failing `POST /v1/group` was sent 3 times → duplicate-create
  risk. Fix: gate the retry loop on `method == "GET"` unless a caller opts in.
- **S3 (Medium-High)** — `NV_ALLOWED_NAMESPACES` is fail-open. `guard.py:90` is
  `if namespace and settings.allowed_namespaces and ...`, so `namespace=None`
  skips it. Of 67 `authorise_write` call sites, **17 pass a real namespace, 50
  pass None** (14 omit the kwarg). Worst instance: `nv_delete_group`
  (`policy_write.py:285`) passes nothing even though `_namespace_from_group_name`
  exists and is used at lines 922/1060/1415. README overstates this control.
- **S5 (Medium)** — `deploy/deployment.yaml` NetworkPolicy ingress has no `from:`
  selector, so every pod in the cluster can reach :8080. The comment above it
  claims "Nothing else, in or out."
- **S6 / Q2 (Medium)** — `NV_AUDIT_LOG_PATH` is documented in README:212 and
  never implemented (parsed, validated, never read). `NV_MAX_RESPONSE_CHARS` is
  documented as a per-result truncation budget but is used only at
  `events.py:290` for threat packet payloads. `audit.redact()` and
  `Settings.redacted()` are dead code (tests only).
- **S4 (Medium)** — FastMCP's own `StaticTokenVerifier` docstring says "Never use
  this in production". No token expiry, no rotation, no rate limit.
- **S7 (Low-Med)** — `NV_VERIFY_TLS: "false"` in the deployed ConfigMap.
- **P2 (Medium)** — re-login stampede. `client.py:255` takes `_login_lock` then
  calls `login()` with no double-check. Proven: 10 concurrent 401s → 10
  `POST /v1/auth`. Risks `ERR_TOO_MANY_LOGIN_USER`. Fix is ~3 lines: snapshot
  `self._token` before the lock, compare after acquiring.
- **P3 (Medium)** — `modes.verify_applied` is N services × 8 attempts of
  sequential GETs with 0.5s sleeps. 20 services ≈ 160 round trips. The codebase
  uses zero `asyncio.gather`.
- **Q3 (Low)** — `build_query` rejects any filter value containing a comma:
  `{"name": "team,alpha"}` raises "unknown operator 'team'".
- **Q4–Q7 (Low)** — 9 duplicated `ToolAnnotations` blocks, 3 copies of
  `_namespace_from_group_name`, 15 function-level imports in `src/`, unvalidated
  `getattr(logging, log_level)`, and `.coverage 2` untracked (`.gitignore`'s
  `.coverage` does not match it).

## Decisions made (and why)

- **S2 fixed centrally, not per-site.** One `validate_path()` call in
  `client.request` rather than editing 63 f-strings. A central reject closes
  traversal and `?`/`#` injection completely in one file with no risk of a bad
  mechanical edit. Per-site encoding would have been a second pass; judged not
  worth it, see next point.
- **`/` stays legal in a name.** A registry image id genuinely is a repository
  path (`.../image/library/api:1.4.2`). Residual: a name with `/` can select a
  *deeper* route under the same prefix (`nv_delete_registry("reg/scan")` hits
  `DELETE /v1/scan/registry/reg/scan`). That cannot escalate — going *up* needs
  `..`, which is refused. Documented in the `validate_path` docstring.
- **S1 resolved by removing scopes, not enforcing them.** Rick's reasoning,
  verbatim: *"The scope should be left to the token. You don't want enforcement
  in multiple, unconnected places. That's horrendous to debug."* Confirmed with
  him that this meant drop the concept, not enforce it at one choke point.
  Privilege now comes from the NeuVector API key's role, narrowed by
  `NV_READ_ONLY`, `NV_TOOLSETS` and the confirm handshake. Two clients needing
  different power = two Deployments.
- **A legacy `<token>:<scope>` value is a startup error, not silently stripped.**
  Stripping preserves belief in a control that never existed; keeping it makes
  the whole string the token and 401s everything. Loud was chosen on purpose.
  This is the deploy blocker below.
- **SPEC N3 ("copy reference/ verbatim") treated as superseded.** It is not
  gate-enforced, and `client.py`, `config.py`, `guard.py` had already drifted
  from `neuvector-mcp-spec/reference/`. Changed `src/`, left `reference/` alone.
- **`SPEC.md` and `neuvector-mcp-spec/` deliberately not edited**, even though
  `SPEC.md:260` still documents the old scope format. Editing the spec to match
  the code inverts which is authoritative. Flagged to Rick, his call.

## Files touched

- `src/neuvector_mcp/client.py` — +76. New `validate_path()` (module-level,
  exported) + one call at the top of `NeuVectorClient.request`. Rejects
  non-`/v1|/v2` paths, `..`/`.` segments (checked against the literal path *and*
  `unquote(path)`), and `?`/`#`/backslash/whitespace/control chars.
- `src/neuvector_mcp/config.py` — `http_bearer_tokens` is now `tuple[str, ...]`
  not `dict[str, list[str]]`. New `_plain_tokens` field validator rejecting `:`.
  `load_settings()` now wraps `Settings(...)` in try/except and re-raises
  `ConfigError` built from `exc.errors(include_input=False, include_url=False)`
  with `from None` — the `from None` matters, chaining would reprint the leak.
  `ConfigError` is a function-level import to keep the module standalone.
- `src/neuvector_mcp/server.py` — `_auth_provider` builds
  `{token: {"client_id": ...}}` with no `scopes`; docstring and `ConfigError`
  message updated.
- `tests/test_path_safety.py` — **new**, 28 tests.
- `tests/test_config.py` — 6 `pytest.raises(ValidationError)` → `ConfigError`
  (only the ones wrapping `load_settings()`; direct `Settings()` construction
  still raises `ValidationError`). New parametrised leak guard across 4
  rejection routes + a password-mode case + a scope-suffix case.
- `README.md` — bearer-token format table row, the format paragraph (now with a
  migration note), and the `NV_HTTP_BEARER_TOKENS` config-table row.
- `deploy/deployment.yaml` — `bearer-tokens: "REPLACE_ME_32_BYTE_HEX"` and an
  expanded comment on why a token does not carry privilege.

## What's verified vs assumed

Verified by running it:
- Full gate green after every change. Final: 680 passed / 1 xfailed, 97.65%.
- S2 before/after — the original exploit PoCs were re-run against the patched
  tree. The two S2 exploits now fail; the S3 ×2 and P1 PoCs still pass, i.e.
  those findings genuinely remain.
- S1 — real uvicorn server on 127.0.0.1:8399: 401 with no token, `tools/list`
  and `nv_delete_group` both work with a plain token. Verifier construction did
  not break auth.
- S9 — a suffixed-token startup failure with `NV_API_SECRET_KEY=SUPER-SECRET`
  set produces a `ConfigError` with the secret absent from the message.
- P1, P2, P3 measurements are all from executed PoCs, not inference. The
  scratchpad PoCs are at
  `/private/tmp/claude-501/.../9008cdb2-.../scratchpad/test_poc.py` and
  `test_scope.py` — session-scoped, they will be gone. Rewriting them is ~20
  minutes if needed.

Assumed, never checked:
- Whether the NeuVector controller decodes `%2F` back into `/` and re-splits
  path segments. Irrelevant to the fix as built (traversal is rejected before
  encoding matters), but it is why per-site `quote(safe="")` was *not* chosen.
- Whether `GET /v1/scan/registry/{name}/image/{id}` is ever called with a
  repository path containing `/` in practice. Assumed yes, which is why `/`
  stays legal. Fixture `tests/fixtures/registry_images.json` shows
  `repository: library/api` alongside `image_id: sha256:aaa111`, so both shapes
  exist upstream.
- The live cluster was never touched. No `kubectl`, no NeuVector MCP tool calls.

## Next step

**Tell Rick to fix the Secret before any rollout** (already surfaced in chat,
repeat it if the new session starts by deploying). The live
`Secret/neuvector-mcp-clients` value carries a `:nv:read` suffix, which is now a
startup error → CrashLoopBackOff:

```bash
kubectl -n neuvector-mcp create secret generic neuvector-mcp-clients \
  --from-literal=bearer-tokens="$(kubectl -n neuvector-mcp get secret neuvector-mcp-clients \
     -o jsonpath='{.data.bearer-tokens}' | base64 -d | cut -d: -f1)" \
  --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
```

Then the agreed queue, in order: **P1** (gate the retry loop on GET), then **S3**
(wire `_namespace_from_group_name` into `nv_delete_group` at
`policy_write.py:285`, then decide whether `guard.py`'s fail-open `if namespace`
should become fail-closed for namespace-scopable operations). Rick confirmed
both have a single correct answer and need no decision from him.

Run `make verify` after each. It is `lint types test spec` and takes ~3 min,
dominated by the test suite.
